items.headline: OpenAI begins unifying ChatGPT's Chat and Work usage into one meter
items.summary: OpenAI has started rolling out a merged Chat and Work experience in ChatGPT to a small group of Pro subscribers, meaning heavy users may draw down the same usage quota across both modes instead of separate allowances.

items.headline: OpenAI to merge ChatGPT and Codex usage allowances starting in December
items.summary: A Help Center notice says Plus, Pro and Business plans will share a single usage pool between ChatGPT and Codex beginning in December, with Instant chat staying outside the shared pool; the combined remaining allowance will show in Settings.

items.headline: Anthropic says it ported Claude's core API from Python to Rust, cutting CPU use up to 50%
items.summary: Anthropic reported that an AI-assisted rewrite of the Messages API that routes every Claude conversation from Python to Rust reduced CPU usage by roughly 40-50% in production, though outside analysts caution some of the gain may reflect general restructuring rather than Rust itself.

items.headline: OpenAI doubles ChatGPT Pro usage limits after subscriber backlash
items.summary: OpenAI reversed a planned 50% cut to usage limits for its $100-$500 ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium tiers, doubling allowances instead after users objected to the proposed reduction.

items.headline: AMD to invest $1 billion in Meta as its Helios AI racks go live there
items.summary: AMD said it will invest $1 billion in Meta's equity offering as the companies deepen an AI infrastructure partnership, with initial AMD Helios rack-scale systems, built around a custom Instinct GPU for Meta, now installed and being tested ahead of broader deployment.

items.headline: New York enacts law banning AI chatbots that pose as human with children
items.summary: Governor Kathy Hochul signed legislation barring companies from offering AI chatbot features to minors that impersonate humans, foster emotional dependency, or encourage self-harm; the law takes effect January 1, 2027 and allows penalties including forced shutdowns.

items.headline: 40 state attorneys general demand child-safety protections in Character.AI bankruptcy sale
items.summary: A coalition led by New York's attorney general asked the Delaware bankruptcy court overseeing Character Technologies' Chapter 11 case to require that any buyer honor privacy protections, data-use limits and ad opt-outs for the chatbot platform's users, many of whom are minors.

items.headline: DeepSeek opens Search and Fetch APIs to outside developers with V4.1-Flash update
items.summary: DeepSeek released an updated V4.1-Flash model and, for the first time, opened its Search and Fetch retrieval APIs to third-party developers at $0.75 per 1,000 calls, intensifying competition with OpenAI and Anthropic on agentic tooling.

items.headline: OpenAI unveils 'Private Intelligence' suite to keep enterprise prompts confidential
items.summary: OpenAI detailed a package of enterprise privacy tools, including Private Inference, a confidential-computing option meant to let businesses run prompts without OpenAI able to read them, alongside zero-data-retention workflows and an optional enterprise key-management layer.

items.headline: FCC reviewing SpaceX plan for up to 1 million orbital AI data-center satellites
items.summary: The FCC has accepted for review a SpaceX filing that could eventually put as many as one million AI-compute satellites in orbit, intended to run AI workloads in space on solar power and transmit results back to Earth; the agency has not yet approved the proposal.

items.headline: Figure's Helix 2.5 robot model completes household tasks zero-shot in 30 unseen homes
items.summary: Figure AI said its updated Helix 2.5 vision-language-action model, pretrained on the company's large 'Index' behavior dataset, succeeded at everyday manipulation tasks without retraining across 30 Bay Area homes it had never seen, part of the broader push toward general-purpose home robots.
